title: E2Former-V2: On-the-Fly Equivariant Attention with Linear Activation Memory
abstract:
Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have become a widely used approach for modeling 3D atomistic systems. However, mainstream architectures face critical efficiency bottlenecks due to the explicit construction of geometric features or dense tensor products on \textit{every} edge. To overcome this, we introduce \textbf{E2Former-V2}, an efficient architecture that integrates algebraic sparsity with hardware-aware execution.
We introduce \textbf{Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS)}, which leverages an $\mathrm{SO}(3)\!\rightarrow\!\mathrm{SO}(2)$ change of basis to convert dense Wigner-$6j$ tensor contractions into sparse, parity-based re-indexing operations.
Building on this representation, we propose \textbf{On-the-Fly Equivariant Attention}, a fully node-centric mechanism implemented via a fused Triton kernel.
By eliminating materialized edge tensors and maximizing SRAM utilization, our kernel achieves up to \textbf{20$\times$ higher TFLOPS} than standard implementations.
Experiments on SPICE and OMol25 show that E2Former-V2 preserves predictive accuracy while substantially accelerating inference, demonstrating the practical feasibility of large equivariant transformers on commodity GPUs. Our released code can be found at \url{https://github.com/IQuestLab/UBio-MolFM/tree/main}
problem: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks face efficiency bottlenecks from explicit construction of geometric features and dense tensor products on every edge, limiting scalability.
approach: E2Former-V2 integrates algebraic sparsity using Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) that converts dense Wigner-6j contractions into sparse operations, implemented via fused Triton kernels for hardware-aware execution.
contribution: Up to 20× higher TFLOPS than standard implementations while preserving predictive accuracy on molecular benchmarks.
